claims.text: An ab initio framework using deep-learning potentials can improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation of atomic configurations will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed intervention is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures.
The exact reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is uncertain and requires calculation and validation.
A comparison against TOR-TILD's EAM references can test whether deep-learning potentials reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
